在仓库 /home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/ 中，这是 BK7258 OpenVela SMP 移植对原厂 Armino CP 固件的覆盖副本。

请阅读以下文件的完整内容，理解每一处的修改目的、改动幅度（小幅补丁还是大改），并简明总结每个文件"做了什么"。这些文件是 SMP/480MHz/电源生命周期方案要求修改的核心 CP 文件：

1. projects/app_ab/cp/cp_main.c - 重点找 OpenVela boot transaction、CONFIG_OPENVELA_AP_480M、user_app_main 相关
2. projects/app_ab/cp/config/bk7258/config - 完整列出所有配置行
3. cp/components/bk_pm/pm.c - 重点找 DVFS 错误传播、VDDDIG 仲裁、vote cache rollback、bk_pm_module_vote_cpu_freq、bk_pm_current_max_cpu_freq_get、PM_DEV_ID_CPU1 相关函数。文件可能很大，搜索关键函数即可
4. cp/components/bk_startup/system_main.c - 重点找 CPU1/CPU2 reset helper（cpu_hold_reset/cpu_release_reset）、start_cpu1_core/start_cpu2_core、run-status readback
5. cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c - 重点找 OpenVela boot transaction、rollback、recovery、shutdown、PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD、PM_OPENVELA_READY_CMD
6. cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/low_pwr_core.c - 重点找 CPU1 exit-sleep vote、OpenVela ready worker、PSRAM V1 protocol
7. cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/Kconfig - 完整列出新增的 CONFIG 项
8. cp/include/driver/pwr_clk.h - 重点找 OpenVela lifecycle API、PM 诊断接口、PSRAM V1
9. cp/include/driver/low_pwr_core.h - OpenVela ready worker 事件
10. cp/include/components/system.h - CPU reset 语义化接口
11. cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/hal/sys_hal.c - 重点找 sys_hal_core_bus_clock_ctrl、sys_hal_switch_cpu_bus_freq、bus divider bit 6、readback（搜索这些函数名，文件很大）
12. cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/include/sys_hal.h - VDDD/VDDDIG readback API
13. cp/middleware/driver/sys_ctrl/sys_ps_driver.c - 单目标 DVFS 切换、错误传播
14. cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_heartbeat.c - heartbeat watchdog 配置符号
15. cp/middleware/driver/psram/psram_driver.c - PSRAM init 失败清理
16. cp/middleware/arch/cm33/trap_base.c - 崩溃 fail-stop reset hold

对每个文件请用 2-4 行说明：(a) 修改的核心内容，(b) 是否明显是为了 SMP/480MHz/电源生命周期，(c) 改动幅度估计（小补丁/中改/大改/几乎重写）。

请用 thoroughness=very thorough。最终返回一个结构化的总结，按文件分组。不要修改任何文件。

180:  * 
181:  * Since AP side is an SMP system, when AP subsystem enters exception, it first acquires SMP system spinlock,

183:  * algorithm (shared memory) to implement spinlock protection between AP and CP.
184:     ________________________________________
185:     1. Objectives
186:     • SMP CP/AP share a section of SRAM (fixed address), when any subsystem enters exception:
187:     o First arrival monopolizes UART → DUMP system info → direct reboot (without releasing lock);
188:     o Later arrival waits permanently (WFE()), avoiding UART conflicts.
189:     • Ensure reliable fallback solution even when shared area is corrupted.
190: 
191:     ________________________________________
192:     2. Shared memory layout (fixed address macros)
193:     • MAGIC_BEGIN / MAGIC_END: Header/tail magic numbers for validating shared area legitimacy.
194:     • CP_EXCEPTION_STATUS / AP_EXCEPTION_STATUS: Peterson's want[0]/want[1].
195:     • EXCEPTION_TURN: turn in Peterson algorithm.
196:     • EXCEPTION_DUMPER: marks who holds the lock (0=CP, 1=AP, -1=none); also used for "first come first serve DUMP" in fallback.
197:     ________________________________________
198: 
199:  */
200: 
201: /* ================= Utility functions ================= */
202: static inline void dmb_ish(void){ __asm volatile("dmb ish" ::: "memory"); }
203: static inline void cpu_wfe(void){ __asm volatile("wfe" ::: "memory"); }
204: static inline void cpu_sev(void){ __asm volatile("sev" ::: "memory"); }
205: 
206: /* ================= Validation / Repair ================= */
207: static inline int values_sane(void){
208:     uint32_t w_cp = FIXED_ADDR_CP_EXCEPTION_STATUS;
209:     uint32_t w_ap = FIXED_ADDR_AP_EXCEPTION_STATUS;
210:     uint32_t turn = FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_TURN;
211:     uint32_t  dump = FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_DUMPER;
212:     if (!((w_cp==0u || w_cp==1u) && (w_ap==0u || w_ap==1u))) return 0;
213:     if (!(turn==0u || turn==1u)) return 0;
214:     if (!(dump== TRAP_DEFAULT_DUMPER || dump==0 || dump==1)) return 0;
215:     return 1;
216: }
217: 
218: 
219: static inline int shared_valid(void){
220:     if (FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_MAGIC_BEGIN != TRAP_DEFAULT_MAGIC_HEAD) return 0;
221:     if (FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_MAGIC_END   != TRAP_DEFAULT_MAGIC_TAIL) return 0;
222:     if (!values_sane()) return 0;
223:     return 1;
224: }
225: static inline int shared_repair(void){
226:     /* Re-seal header/tail + clear key fields (write header→clear values→write tail), with memory barrier for visibility */
227:     FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_MAGIC_BEGIN = TRAP_DEFAULT_MAGIC_HEAD;
228:     dmb_ish();
229:     FIXED_ADDR_CP_EXCEPTION_STATUS = 0u;
230:     FIXED_ADDR_AP_EXCEPTION_STATUS = 0u;
231:     FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_TURN      = 0u;
232:     FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_DUMPER    = TRAP_DEFAULT_DUMPER; /* -1 */
233:     dmb_ish();
234:     FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_MAGIC_END = TRAP_DEFAULT_MAGIC_TAIL;
235:     dmb_ish();
236:     return shared_valid();
237: }
238: 
239: 
240: /* Is current Dump owner:
241:  * Returns: 1 = CP is current dump owner, 0 = CP is not current dump owner
242:  * Note: Even if magic area is corrupted, as long as DUMPER is correctly written to 0/1 (including fallback logic),
243:  *       it can accurately return the owner.
244:  */
245:  static inline int is_cp_in_dump_mode(void){
246:     __asm volatile("dmb ish" ::: "memory");
247:     uint32_t dumper = FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_DUMPER;
248:     __asm volatile("dmb ish" ::: "memory");
249:     if (dumper == TRAP_DEFAULT_DUMPER) return 0;          /* Clearly not held */
250:     if (FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_MAGIC_BEGIN != TRAP_DEFAULT_MAGIC_HEAD) return 0;
251:     if (FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_MAGIC_END   != TRAP_DEFAULT_MAGIC_TAIL) return 0;
252: 
253:     if (dumper == 0) return 1;
254: 
255:     return 0;
256: }
257: 
258: /* Is current Dump owner:
259:  * Returns: 1 = AP is current dump owner, 0 = AP is not current dump owner
260:  * Note: Even if magic area is corrupted, as long as DUMPER is correctly written to 0/1 (including fallback logic),
261:  *       it can accurately return the owner.
262:  */
263: static inline int is_ap_in_dump_mode(void){
264:     __asm volatile("dmb ish" ::: "memory");
265:     uint32_t dumper = FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_DUMPER;
266:     __asm volatile("dmb ish" ::: "memory");
267:     if (dumper == TRAP_DEFAULT_DUMPER) return 0;          /* Clearly not held */
268:     if (FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_MAGIC_BEGIN != TRAP_DEFAULT_MAGIC_HEAD) return 0;
269:     if (FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_MAGIC_END   != TRAP_DEFAULT_MAGIC_TAIL) return 0;
270: 
271:     if (dumper == 1) return 1;
272: 
273:     return 0;
274: }

277: /* ================= Power-on/Reset early initialization ================= */
278: void exception_sync_init_early(void){
279:     (void)shared_repair();
280:     dmb_ish();
281: }
282: /* ================= Peterson lock (volatile + DMB, symmetric) ================= */
283: static inline void peterson_lock(unsigned me){
284:     unsigned other = (me ^ 1u);
285:     FIXED_ADDR_CP_EXCEPTION_STATUS = 1u;               /* I want to enter */
286:     FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_TURN = other;/* Give priority to the other */
287:     dmb_ish();                        /* Flush write buffer + establish ordering */
288:     while ((FIXED_ADDR_AP_EXCEPTION_STATUS == 1u) && (FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_TURN == other)){
289:         cpu_wfe();                    /* Wait for the other to yield/exit */
290:     }
291:     /* Enter critical section */
292: }
293: /* ================= Fallback (current CPU directly DUMP; other core waits permanently) ================= */
294: static inline void fallback_take_and_dump(unsigned me){
295:     /* Grab fallback ownership: write DUMPER as me; if read back is not me, other side got it first → wait permanently */
296:     FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_DUMPER = me;
297:     dmb_ish();
298:     if (FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_DUMPER != me){
299:         for(;;) cpu_wfe();            /* Avoid UART conflicts */
300:     }
301: }
302: /* ================= Unified exception handling (shared by both cores) ================= */
303: static void exception_get_peterson_lock(unsigned me /*CP_ID/AP_ID*/){
304:     __disable_irq();
305:     dmb_ish();
306:     /* Shared area corrupted/uninitialized → try to repair; if repair fails → fallback (current core directly DUMP, other core waits) */
307:     if (!shared_valid()){
308:         if (!shared_repair()){
309:             fallback_take_and_dump(me);
310:         } else {
311:             /* Normal path: Peterson mutual exclusion enter exception critical section */
312:             peterson_lock(me);
313:             /* Declare me as critical section holder (also used as fallback placeholder reuse, no additional field) */
314:             FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_DUMPER = me;
315:         }
316:     } else {
317:         /* Normal path: Peterson mutual exclusion enter exception critical section */
318:         peterson_lock(me);
319:         /* Declare me as critical section holder (also used as fallback placeholder reuse, no additional field) */
320:         FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_DUMPER = me;
321:     }
322: 
323:     dmb_ish();
324:     cpu_sev(); /* Wake up the other side to make it quickly stuck in the waiting loop */
325: }

577: static void dump_context(uint32_t lr, uint32_t msp)
578: {
579:     SAVED_CONTEXT regs;
580: 
581:     regs.r4 = ((uint32_t *)msp)[-8];
582:     regs.r5 = ((uint32_t *)msp)[-7];
583:     regs.r6 = ((uint32_t *)msp)[-6];
584:     regs.r7 = ((uint32_t *)msp)[-5];
585:     regs.r8 = ((uint32_t *)msp)[-4];
586:     regs.r9 = ((uint32_t *)msp)[-3];
587:     regs.r10 = ((uint32_t *)msp)[-2];
588:     regs.r11 = ((uint32_t *)msp)[-1];
589:     regs.control = lr;       // Exception LR.
590: 
591:     regs.msp = __get_MSP();
592:     regs.psp = __get_PSP();
593: 
594:     regs.primask = __get_PRIMASK();
595:     regs.basepri = __get_BASEPRI();
596:     regs.faultmask = __get_FAULTMASK();
597: 
598:     regs.fpscr = __get_FPSCR();
599: 
600: 	uint32_t stack_pointer = msp;
601: 	uint32_t stack_adj = 8 * sizeof(uint32_t);
602: 
603: 	if(lr & (1UL << 2))
604: 	{
605: 		stack_pointer = __get_PSP();
606: 	}
607: 
608: 	if((lr & (1UL << 4)) == 0)
609: 	{
610:         stack_adj += 18 * sizeof(uint32_t);  // 18 FPU registers
611: 	}
612: 
613: 	regs.r0 = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[0];
614: 	regs.r1 = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[1];
615: 	regs.r2 = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[2];
616: 	regs.r3 = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[3];
617: 	regs.r12 = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[4];
618: 	regs.lr = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[5];
619: 	regs.pc = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[6];
620: 	regs.xpsr = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[7];
621: 
622: 	if(regs.xpsr & (1UL << 9))
623: 	{
624: 		stack_adj += 1 * sizeof(uint32_t);
625: 	}
626: 	regs.sp = stack_pointer + stack_adj;
627: 
628:     arch_dump_cpu_registers(0, &regs);
629: }

686: #define CHECK_TASK_WDT_INTERRUPT (0x13)
687: 
688: uint32_t g_wdt_handler_lr = 0;
689: 
690: static void user_except_handler(uint32_t reset_reason, SAVED_CONTEXT *regs)
691: {
692:     if (0 == arch_is_enter_exception()) {
693:         // Make sure the interrupt is disable
694:         uint32_t int_level = port_disable_interrupts_flag();
695:         
696:         /* Handled Trap */
697:         arch_set_enter_exception();
698:         dump_prologue();
699: 
700:         /* set reset reson fisrt to avoid the loss of information due to
701:         abnormalities in the dump process */
702:         bk_misc_set_reset_reason(reset_reason);
703:     #if CONFIG_AON_PMU_REG0_REFACTOR_DEV
704:         aon_pmu_drv_r0_latch_to_r7b();
705:     #endif
706: 
707:         // If it is a task WDT assert!
708:         if((regs->xpsr & 0x1FF) == CHECK_TASK_WDT_INTERRUPT)  // It can be used for any interrupts if LR is saved at entrance of ISR.
709:         {
710:             if(g_wdt_handler_lr & (1UL << 2))
711:             {
712:                 uint32_t stack_pointer = __get_PSP();
713:                 uint32_t stack_adj = 8 * sizeof(uint32_t);
714: 
715:                 if((g_wdt_handler_lr & (1UL << 4)) == 0)
716:                 {
717:                     stack_adj += 18 * sizeof(uint32_t);  // 18 FPU registers
718:                 }
719: 
720:                 regs->r0 = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[0];
721:                 regs->r1 = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[1];
722:                 regs->r2 = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[2];
723:                 regs->r3 = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[3];
724:                 regs->r12 = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[4];
725:                 regs->lr = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[5];
726:                 regs->pc = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[6];
727:                 regs->xpsr = ((uint32_t *)stack_pointer)[7];
728: 
729:                 if(regs->xpsr & (1UL << 9))
730:                 {
731:                     stack_adj += 1 * sizeof(uint32_t);
732:                 }
733:                 regs->sp = stack_pointer + stack_adj;
734:             }
735:         }
736: 
737:         arch_dump_cpu_registers(ECAUSE_ASSERT, regs);
738: 
739:         rtos_dump_system();
740: 
741:         dump_epilogue();
742: 
743:         bk_reboot_ex(reset_reason);
744: 
745:         while(1);
746: 
747:         (void)port_enable_interrupts_flag(int_level);
748:     } else {
749:         BK_DUMP_OUT("CP Secondary crash happend, rr: 0x%x\r\n", reset_reason);
750: 		dump_epilogue();
751:         bk_wdt_force_reboot();
752:     }
753: 
754: }

203: static bk_err_t cpu_reset_wait(uint32_t cpu_id, uint32_t released)
204: {
205: 	uint32_t count = 1000;
206: 
207: 	while (count--)
208: 	{
209: 		uint32_t control = cpu_id == 1 ?
210: 			sys_ll_get_cpu1_int_halt_clk_op_cpu1_sw_rst() :
211: 			sys_ll_get_cpu2_int_halt_clk_op_cpu2_sw_rst();
212: 		uint32_t status = cpu_id == 1 ?
213: 			sys_ll_get_cpu_current_run_status_cpu1_sw_reset() :
214: 			sys_ll_get_cpu_current_run_status_cpu2_sw_reset();
215: 
216: 		if (control == released && status == released)
217: 			return BK_OK;
218: 		bk_delay_us(1);
219: 	}
220: 
221: 	BK_LOGE(NULL, "cpu%d reset %s failed ctrl=0x%x run=0x%x\r\n",
222: 		cpu_id, released ? "release" : "hold",
223: 		cpu_id == 1 ? bk_cpu1_ctrl_get() : bk_cpu2_ctrl_get(),
224: 		bk_cpu_run_status_get());
225: 	return BK_FAIL;
226: }

159: static bk_err_t low_pwr_core_message_handle(void)
160: {
161:     bk_err_t ret = BK_OK;
162:     low_pwr_core_msg_t msg;
163: 
164:     while (1)
165:     {
166:         ret = rtos_pop_from_queue(&s_pm_info->queue, &msg, BEKEN_WAIT_FOREVER);
167: 		LOGV("LP event:%d\n", msg.event);
168:         if (kNoErr == ret)
169:         {
170:             switch (msg.event)
171:             {
172:                 case LOW_PWR_CORE_STATE_ENTER_DEEPSLEEP:
173:                 {
174: 					bk_pm_cp0_response_cp1(PM_ENTER_DEEP_SLEEP_CMD,BK_OK,0,0);
175: 					bk_pm_sleep_mode_set(msg.param1);
176:                 }
177:                 break;
178: 				case LOW_PWR_CORE_CTRL_CP2_STATE:
179: 				{
180: 					bk_pm_cp0_response_cp1(PM_CTRL_AP_STATE_CMD, BK_OK,0,0);
181: 					bk_pm_module_vote_boot_cp1_ctrl(msg.param1,msg.param2);
182: 				}
183: 				break;
184: 				case LOW_PWR_CORE_CP2_RECOVERY:
185: 				{
186: 					bk_pm_cp1_recovery_module_state_ctrl(msg.param1,msg.param2);
187: 				}
188: 				break;
189: 				case LOW_PWR_CORE_RTC_DEEPSLEEP:
190: 				{
191: 					bk_pm_cp0_response_cp1(PM_RTC_DEEPSLEEP_CMD, BK_OK,0,0);
192: 					bk_low_pwr_misc_rtc_enter_deepsleep(msg.param2,NULL);
193:                 }
194: 				break;
195: 				case LOW_PWR_CORE_GET_CP_DATA:
196: 				{
197: 					uint32_t cp_pm_data = 0;
198: 					pm_ap_get_cp_data_type_e data_type = msg.param1;
199: 					pm_openvela_diag_t diag;
200: 
201: 					bk_pm_openvela_diag_get(&diag);
202: 					switch(data_type)
203: 					{
204: 						case PM_CP_DATE_TYPE_TIME_INTERVAL_FROM_STARTUP:
205: 							bk_low_pwr_misc_get_time_interval_from_startup(&cp_pm_data);
206: 						break;
207: 						case PM_CP_DATE_TYPE_DEEP_SLEEP_WAKEUP_SOURCE:
208: 							cp_pm_data = bk_pm_deep_sleep_wakeup_source_get();
209: 						break;
210: 						case PM_CP_DATE_TYPE_EXIT_LOW_VOL_WAKEUP_SOURCE:
211: 							cp_pm_data =  bk_pm_exit_low_vol_wakeup_source_get();
212: 						break;
213: 						case PM_CP_DATE_TYPE_CURRENT_FREQUENCY:
214: 							cp_pm_data = (diag.cpu1_vote & 0xff) |
215: 								((diag.max_vote & 0xff) << 8);
216: 						break;
217: 						case PM_CP_DATE_TYPE_CLOCK_DIVIDER:
218: 							cp_pm_data = diag.clk_div_reg0;
219: 						break;
220: 						case PM_CP_DATE_TYPE_CPU_SPEED:
221: 							cp_pm_data = (diag.cpu_speed[0] & 0xff) |
222: 								((diag.cpu_speed[1] & 0xff) << 8) |
223: 								((diag.cpu_speed[2] & 0xff) << 16);
224: 						break;
225: 						case PM_CP_DATE_TYPE_VOLTAGE:
226: 							cp_pm_data = (diag.vddd & 0xffff) |
227: 								((diag.vdddig & 0xffff) << 16);
228: 						break;
229: 						case PM_CP_DATE_TYPE_CPU_POWER_RESET:
230: 							cp_pm_data = (diag.cpu1_power & 0xf) |
231: 								((diag.cpu2_power & 0xf) << 4) |
232: 								((diag.cpu_run_status & 0xffff) << 8);
233: 						break;
234: 						case PM_CP_DATE_TYPE_PSRAM_OWNERS:
235: 							cp_pm_data = diag.psram_owners;
236: 						break;
237: 						default:
238: 						break;
239: 					}
240: 					bk_pm_cp0_response_cp1(PM_GET_PM_DATA_CMD,data_type,cp_pm_data,0);
241: 				}
242: 				break;
243: 				case LOW_PWR_CORE_PSRAM_POWER:
244: 				{
245: 					if (msg.param3 != PM_PSRAM_PROTO_V1 ||
246: 						msg.param1 != PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_NAME_OPENVELA)
247: 						ret = BK_ERR_NOT_SUPPORT;
248: 					else
249: 						ret = bk_pm_module_vote_psram_ctrl(msg.param1,msg.param2);
250: 					bk_pm_cp0_response_cp1(PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD,
251: 						msg.param2, ret, msg.param3);
252: 				}
253: 				break;
254: 				case LOW_PWR_CORE_OPENVELA_READY:
255: 				{
256: 					bk_err_t response_ret;
257: 
258: 					if (msg.param3 != PM_OPENVELA_READY_PROTO_V1)
259: 						ret = BK_ERR_NOT_SUPPORT;
260: 					else
261: 						ret = bk_pm_openvela_ready_handle(msg.param1,
262: 							(int32_t)msg.param2);
263: 					response_ret = bk_pm_cp0_response_cp1(
264: 						PM_OPENVELA_READY_CMD, msg.param1, ret,
265: 						PM_OPENVELA_READY_PROTO_V1);
266: 					if (ret != BK_OK)
267: 						LOGE("OpenVela ready %d failed: %d\r\n",
268: 							msg.param1, ret);
269: 					if (response_ret != BK_OK)
270: 						LOGE("OpenVela ready response failed: %d\r\n",
271: 							response_ret);
272: 				}
273: 				break;
274: 				case LOW_PWR_CORE_POWER_CTRL:
275: 				{
276: 					ret = bk_pm_module_vote_power_ctrl(msg.param1,msg.param2);
277: 					bk_pm_cp0_response_cp1(PM_POWER_CTRL_CMD,ret,0,0);
278: 				}
279: 				break;
280: 				case LOW_PWR_CORE_CLK_CTRL:
281: 				{
282: 					ret = bk_pm_clock_ctrl(msg.param1,msg.param2);
283: 					bk_pm_cp0_response_cp1(PM_CLK_CTRL_CMD, ret,0,0);
284: 				}
285: 				break;
286: 				case LOW_PWR_CORE_SLEEP_CTRL:
287: 				{
288: 					bk_pm_cp0_response_cp1(PM_SLEEP_CTRL_CMD,BK_OK,0,0);
289: 					ret = bk_pm_module_vote_sleep_ctrl(msg.param1,msg.param2,msg.param3);
290: 				}
291: 				break;
292: 				case LOW_PWR_CORE_FREQ_CTRL:
293: 				{
294: 					ret = bk_pm_module_vote_cpu_freq(msg.param1,msg.param2);
295: 					bk_pm_cp0_response_cp1(PM_CPU_FREQ_CTRL_CMD, ret,0,0);
296: 				}
297: 				break;
298: 				case LOW_PWR_CORE_EXTERNAL_LDO:
299: 				{
300: 					ret = bk_pm_module_vote_ctrl_external_ldo(msg.param1,msg.param2,msg.param3);
301: 					bk_pm_cp0_response_cp1(PM_CTRL_EXTERNAL_LDO_CMD, ret,0,0);
302: 				}
303: 				break;
304: 				case LOW_PWR_CORE_WAKEUP_SRC_CFG:

466: 	clk_param = 0;
467: 	clk_param = sys_hal_all_modules_clk_div_get(CLK_DIV_REG0);
468: 	if(((clk_param >> 0x4)&0x3) > cksel_core)//when it from the higher frequency to lower frequency
469: 	{

471: 		clk_param = 0;
472: 		clk_param = sys_hal_all_modules_clk_div_get(CLK_DIV_REG0);
473: 		clk_param &=  ~(0x3 << 4);

478: 		clk_param = 0;

480: 		clk_param &= ~((0xF << 0) | (0x1 << 6));
481: 		clk_param |= (ckdiv_core << 0) | (ckdiv_bus << 6);

495: 		}
496: 
497: 		clk_param = 0;
498: 		clk_param = sys_hal_all_modules_clk_div_get(CLK_DIV_REG0);
499: 		clk_param &= ~((0xF << 0) | (0x1 << 6));
500: 		clk_param |= (ckdiv_core << 0) | (ckdiv_bus << 6);
501: 		sys_hal_all_modules_clk_div_set(CLK_DIV_REG0,clk_param);
502: 
503: 		/*2.config cpu clk div*/
504: 		if(ckdiv_core != 0)
505: 		{
506: 			sys_hal_cpu_clk_div_set(0,ckdiv_cpu0);
507: 		}
508: 		sys_hal_cpu_clk_div_set(1,ckdiv_cpu1);
509: 		sys_hal_cpu_clk_div_set(2,1);//config cpu2
510: 
511: 		/*3.core clk select*/
512: 
513: 		clk_param = 0;

518: 	}

534: 		sys_hal_cpu_clk_div_set(2, old_cpu[2]);
